steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sin is any action that goes against God's will. Christians believe that sin separates humans from God and that all people have a tendency to sin (original sin), which stems from Adam and Eve's disobedience in Genesis 3.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Different Christian traditions emphasise different aspects of salvation. Protestants tend to emphasise grace and faith alone (sola fide), while Catholics emphasise the importance of both faith and good works cooperating with grace.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Sin and Salvation
steps.body: 1. For Sin and Salvation questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Sin and Salvation to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain two Christian beliefs about salvation. | Q: "People can be good without God." Evaluate this statement with reference to Christian teaching.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
